title: QCOM entries, Aug 31 – Sep 11: good or bad?
intro: Twelve QCOM entries from two weeks of trading. Each card shows the setup exactly as it looked at the moment of entry: the daily chart up to the prior close and the 5-minute chart up to the fill. Decide whether to take it before you flip the card. The verdicts use the same rubric the alert monitor and the journal use, plus Tito's trigger and contract rules and your own entry rules.
checklist: 1. Daily chart in play long? The rubric's first gate: if the daily state isn't LONG, the entry grades F.
2. After 10:00? Early entries (before 10:00) grade C at best unless it's an ORB9 breakout.
3. Location: within about 1 ADR of the 21 EMA? 1-2 ADR is where August lost money; beyond 2 is a chase.
4. A trigger, not a wiggle: a close above the 15-day high, a VWAP reclaim, or a deliberate base entry below the high with a planned stop.
5. Vehicle: 3-7 week calls around 0.2-0.35 delta (or a put spread when extended). Never under-a-week calls in size.
6. Exit planned before entry: a stop at a level, no same-day exit unless the stop is hit, sell half at 3x, trail the rest on the 20 EMA.

cards.label: 9/18 180C, 1 contract @2.69
why: ✓ Daily chart in play long (near the 21 EMA, room to the prior high).
✓ A real trigger: QCOM was breaking its 15-day high (168.87) intraday, up 3.2% on the day.
✗ 09:48 is before 10:00, so the rubric grades it C. Early entries lost money in the 20-session alert study.
✗ Already 1.1 ADR above the 21 EMA, the band where August's entries lost.
✓ The contract was reasonable: 18 days, 6% out of the money.
cards.happened: Sold 21 minutes later at 2.06 (−23%) with no stop hit. The same contract printed 4.15 on 9/10, +54% from your entry.
cards.rule: An early entry needs a stop at a level decided in advance. Without one, the first wiggle decides for you.

cards.label: Oct-16 145/155 bull put spread, 1 lot, 2.41 credit
why: ✓ Daily chart in play long, after 10:00: grade B.
✓ With QCOM already 0.9 ADR above the 21 EMA on a +2.6% day, a put spread is long without chasing: 'vehicle follows entry quality'.
✓ Defined risk, short strike 8% out of the money, 46 days: time on your side.
✓ Left alone.
cards.happened: Still open. On 9/10 the spread was worth about 1.29, so roughly 46% of the maximum profit is already captured.
cards.rule: When the stock is already stretched, change the vehicle, not the thesis.

cards.label: Nov-20 195C, 1 contract @6.54
why: ✓ Grade B: daily chart in play, after 10:00, QCOM above VWAP on a breakout day.
✓ Long-dated, 15% out of the money: a patient contract.
✗ The second call on the same idea within an hour (the 180C was sold 30 minutes earlier).
✗ Sold 85 minutes later at 5.98 (−$56; −$58 after commissions), no stop hit.
cards.happened: The same contract printed 10.80 on 9/10: +65% from your entry, had you held.
cards.rule: Decide the vehicle once, before the entry. Switching contracts every hour is a sign there's no plan.

cards.label: Oct-16 185C, 1 contract @4.86
why: ✓ The setup itself still grades B.
✗ The third call on one idea in four hours: churning, not trading.
✗ Sold 42 minutes later at 4.73 (−$13; −$15 after commissions) with nothing broken.
cards.happened: Printed 7.65 on 9/10 (+57% from entry). Each of the three early calls on 8/31 was a fine idea that was sold within the hour.
cards.rule: Three vehicles on one idea means there's no plan. The fills (and the report card) punish it.

cards.label: Oct-2 190C, 1 contract @2.48
why: ✓ Grade B, and QCOM was holding above its 15-day high into the afternoon: the breakout stuck.
✓ Tito's contract: 32 days, 12% out of the money (about 0.2-0.3 delta).
✓ Held through the 9/1 gap-down (−2.8%) and the 9/2 dip without selling.
cards.happened: Held 11 days. Under the scale-out rule it would still be open: it never tripled, and QCOM never closed below its 20 EMA. You sold it on 9/11 to protect the day's gain.
cards.rule: Buy the right contract once, then hold it through the noise. This is the pattern to repeat.

cards.label: 9/4 170C, 10 contracts @0.78
why: ✗ Daily chart OUT of play: 8/31's run left QCOM 1.2 ADR above the 21 EMA. Grade F.
✗ A bounce on a gap-down day (−2.8% open, −3.8% at entry), 4.3% below the 15-day high.
✗ 3 days to expiry, 10 contracts: lottery tickets in size.
cards.happened: Sold 42 minutes later at 0.82 (+$40; +$31 after commissions). The 9/4 170C expired worthless: QCOM closed 168.74 that day. The profit was luck.
cards.rule: Under a week to expiry is a coin flip with decay. Never size it up.

cards.label: 9/11 172.5C, 1 contract @1.68
why: ✗ Same day, same problem: daily chart out of play, grade F.
✗ 3.3% below the 15-day high on a gap-down day: a dip buy with no trigger.
✓ The exit was fine: sold the next afternoon at 2.64 (+57%).
cards.happened: It made money. That's the danger: a win from a bad entry teaches the wrong lesson. (It printed 5.23 on 9/10, after the 9/8 breakout.)
cards.rule: Grade the entry, not the outcome. The journal graded this F even though it won.

cards.label: 100 shares @166.87
why: ✗ Daily chart out of play: grade F.
✗ Bought in the last 35 minutes of the day, with no level for a stop.
✗ Sold 6 minutes later at 166.41 (−$46).
cards.happened: A classic noise round trip: in and out inside six minutes, nothing broken, nothing learned.
cards.rule: No entry without a stop, and no same-day exit unless the stop is hit.

cards.label: 9/4 172.5C, 10 contracts @0.88
why: ✗ Grade F: the same out-of-play daily chart.
✗ Stock and calls on the same idea within two minutes: two vehicles, doubled risk.
✗ 3 days to expiry, 10 contracts, and half sold 3 minutes later.
cards.happened: Sold in four pieces over two days: −$55 in total (−$65 after commissions). It expired worthless on 9/4.
cards.rule: One vehicle per idea. If you can't choose between the stock and the calls, the setup isn't clear enough.

cards.label: 9/18 177.5C, 1 contract @2.66
why: ✗ Daily chart OUT: 'no room', only 0.1 ADR under the prior high. Grade F.
✗ Sold the next morning at 09:57 for 1.68 (−37%), before 10:00 and at no level.
cards.happened: Five sessions later QCOM broke out (9/8: +6.9% gap on 2.9x volume). This contract printed 5.35 on 9/10: +101% from your entry. Bad entry, then a panic exit right before it would have paid.
cards.rule: If you buy early, you have to be able to hold early. Size so the stop is a level, not a feeling.

cards.label: 15 shares @168.97
why: ✓ Grade B: daily chart in play (near the rising 21 EMA), after 10:00.
✗ Token size (15 shares), no stated plan, sold at the close for a scratch.
cards.happened: Flat. A B setup traded like a C.
cards.rule: If the setup is a B, size it like one or skip it. Token positions just add fills.

cards.label: Nov-20 200C, 1 contract @4.92
why: ✓ Grade B: daily chart in play, only 0.6 ADR above a rising 21 EMA. Tight location.
✓ A base entry: 2.1% below the 15-day high, one session before the breakout.
✓ Tito's contract: 19% out of the money, about 0.2 delta, 77 days.
✓ Held.
cards.happened: The next session QCOM gapped 6.9% and closed above the 15-day high on 2.9x volume. On 9/11 the call closed at 9.81: 2.0x. Plan: trail QCOM's 20 EMA; a GTC to sell at 3x (~14.75).
cards.rule: The best entry was the quietest one: at the base, before the crowd, with the right contract, and then left alone.
